candidate_evidence.quote: oral ropidoxuridine as a radiation-sensitizing agent

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Newly Diagnosed IDH-Wildtype Glioblastoma With Unmethylated MGMT Promoter

tumour_pk_planned_evidence.quote: Maximum plasma concentration for orally administered ropidoxuridine, at dose levels of 960 and 1200 mg once daily.

role_evidence.quote: oral ropidoxuridine as a radiation-sensitizing agent
Ropidoxuridine is administered orally at 960 mg, 5 days a week for a total of 7 weeks, starting 1 week before the initiation of radiotherapy.

source_quote.quote: Histologically confirmed supratentorial glioblastoma isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type classification (2021 World Health Organization Classification of Tumours, 5th Edition, Volume 6)
with unmethylated O6-methylguanine-DNA-methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter (defined as MGMT methylation status ≤20% by pyrosequencing

coder_notes: Ropidoxuridine given with 60 Gy radiotherapy, so regimen is combination while the drug is the only investigational agent (experimental_monotherapy). Both experimental arms are dose levels; efficacy compared with historical controls, no registered control arm. Temozolomide/Optune maintenance is at investigator discretion, not given to all, so not listed. MGMT unmethylated is an eligibility requirement but not candidate-matched.
